text: Brand impersonation occurs when an attacker pretends to represent a trusted company or organization to make a malicious message, website, or request appear legitimate.

A common brand impersonation indicator is a domain that looks similar to a legitimate organization's domain but contains misspellings, extra words, altered characters, or an unrelated top-level domain.
Attackers may copy a legitimate company's logo, colors, wording, email style, login page, or website design to make fraudulent content appear authentic.

Bank impersonation scams may claim that an account has a security problem, suspicious activity, payment issue, or verification requirement and then request credentials, codes, or financial information.
Cloud service impersonation may imitate services such as Microsoft, Google, Apple, or other technology providers and request users to verify an account, reset a password, or review a security alert.

Government impersonation scams may claim to represent tax authorities, law enforcement, immigration services, courts, or other government organizations and use threats, fines, or urgent deadlines to pressure victims.
Social media impersonation may imitate platforms or individual accounts and ask users to click a verification link, provide login credentials, share authentication codes, or make a payment.

When a message claims to represent a trusted brand, users should verify the sender, domain, and request through the organization's official website or another independently trusted communication channel.
